skill.name: azure-cost
skill.description: Query Azure Cost Management data, forecast future spend, and build optimization reports using Azure APIs, CLI commands, and best-practice guidance.
skill.summary: Analyze Azure spending, forecasts, and cost optimization opportunities with guided Azure workflows.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: No prompt-injection language, malicious data exfiltration, or business-logic abuse was found in the reviewed files. The static findings are false positives from Markdown links, code fences, official Azure endpoints, Azure CLI examples, and credential best-practice snippets.

remediation.issue: Azure CLI examples can access subscription cost and resource metadata when a user runs them.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands require explicit user approval and should use least-privilege Cost Management Reader access.

remediation.issue: Generated reports and saved query results may contain cost amounts, resource IDs, and subscription identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to redact sensitive identifiers before sharing reports outside the user organization.

content.value_statement: Azure cost data is hard to query, forecast, and explain across scopes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Azure cost analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides historical Azure cost queries by subscription, resource group, management group, or billing scope.
Builds forecast workflows for future spending with date, granularity, and response guardrails.
Supports cost breakdowns by service, resource, location, tag, or supported billing dimensions.
Documents Azure CLI, REST API, and Azure MCP tool usage for cost analysis.
Helps prepare optimization reports with actual costs, utilization metrics, pricing checks, and recommendations.
Includes error handling, pagination guidance, rate-limit behavior, and API validation rules.
limitations: Requires authenticated Azure access and appropriate read permissions on the selected scope.
Does not deploy resources or estimate costs for resources that do not exist yet.
Forecast quality depends on available historical cost data and Azure forecast API support.
Optimization recommendations still need human review before any operational change.

use_cases.title: Explain Monthly Spend
use_cases.description: Break down current Azure spend by service, resource group, tag, or supported billing dimension.

use_cases.title: Forecast Budget Risk
use_cases.description: Project end-of-month Azure costs and identify when forecast data is incomplete or unavailable.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Savings Work
use_cases.description: Find orphaned resources, rightsizing candidates, and service-specific optimization opportunities using actual cost data.

prompt_templates.title: Show Current Spend
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my Azure spending for this month by service. Ask for the scope if I have not provided one.

prompt_templates.title: Forecast Month-End Cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Forecast my end-of-month Azure cost for subscription <subscription-id>. Include assumptions and unavailable data warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Find Optimization Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure costs and resource utilization for the last 30 days. Prioritize savings by impact, risk, and required approval.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Executive Cost Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Azure cost optimization report using actual cost data, utilization metrics, and validated pricing. Include audit trail notes and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: Show my Azure cost by service for this month.
output: Monthly spend summary with total cost and currency.
Ranked service breakdown with top cost drivers.
Notes about scope, date range, and any missing permissions.
Forecast total with actual and projected periods separated.
Confidence notes based on available historical data.
Warnings when the Azure forecast API cannot produce rows.

output_examples.input: Find cost savings in my subscription.
output: Prioritized savings list with estimated monthly impact.
Evidence from actual cost data and utilization metrics.
Approval notes, rollback guidance, and validation steps.

best_practices: Start with read-only cost queries before making optimization recommendations.
Confirm scope, role permissions, timeframe, and billing agreement before selecting dimensions.
Validate pricing and free-tier rules with official Azure sources before estimating savings.
anti_patterns: Do not estimate Azure spend from memory when actual cost data is available.
Do not run cleanup or deletion commands without explicit user approval.
Do not trust forecast results when the API reports insufficient history.

faq.question: What permissions are needed?
faq.answer: Users need Cost Management Reader and related read permissions on the selected Azure scope.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy or delete resources?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on cost analysis, forecasting, and recommendations. Any operational change needs separate approval.

faq.question: Does it use actual Azure billing data?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows prioritize Azure Cost Management API data instead of assumptions.

faq.question: Can it forecast future spend?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the Azure forecast API, but forecasts need enough historical cost data.

faq.question: Which tools can it use?
faq.answer: It documents Azure MCP tools, Azure CLI commands, REST API calls, and selected SDK references.

faq.question: Will reports contain sensitive data?
faq.answer: Reports can include costs, resource IDs, and subscription identifiers. Review and redact them before sharing.
